{{Separation axioms}}

In [[mathematics]], particularly [[topology]], a [[topological space]] ''X'' is '''locally normal''' if intuitively it looks locally like a [[normal space]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bella |first1=A. |last2=Carlson |first2=N. |date=2018-01-02 |title=On cardinality bounds involving the weak Lindelöf degree |url=https://doi.org/10.2989/16073606.2017.1373157 |journal=Quaestiones Mathematicae |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=99–113 |doi=10.2989/16073606.2017.1373157 |s2cid=119732758 |issn=1607-3606|url-access=subscription }}</ref> More precisely, a locally normal space satisfies the property that each point of the space belongs to a [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhood]] of the space that is normal under the [[subspace topology]]. 

==Formal definition==

A [[topological space]] ''X'' is said to be locally normal [[if and only if]] each point, ''x'', of ''X'' has a [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhood]] that is [[normal space|normal]] under the [[subspace topology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hansell |first1=R. W. |last2=Jayne |first2=J. E. |last3=Rogers |first3=C. A. |date=June 1985 |title=Separation of K –analytic sets |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/S0025579300010962 |journal=[[Mathematika]] |language=en |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=147–190 |doi=10.1112/S0025579300010962 |issn=0025-5793|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Note that not every neighbourhood of ''x'' has to be normal, but at least one neighbourhood of ''x'' has to be normal (under the subspace topology).

Note however, that if a space were called locally normal [[if and only if]] each point of the space belonged to a subset of the space that was normal under the subspace topology, then every topological space would be locally normal. This is because, the singleton {''x''} is [[Vacuous truth|vacuously]] normal and contains ''x''. Therefore, the definition is more restrictive.

==Examples and properties==

* Every locally normal [[T1 space]] is locally regular and [[Locally Hausdorff space|locally Hausdorff]].
* A [[Locally compact space|locally compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] is always locally normal.
* A normal space is always locally normal.
* A [[T1 space]] need not be locally normal as the set of all real numbers endowed with the [[cofinite topology]] shows.
